problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ If ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-7{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=4{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1},$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C.$
worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
